steps.message:
Using hyperpowers:using-hyperpowers — this lands on rung 1 of the ladder (removing an auth check), so I'm flagging the consequence before touching anything.

**What the change would do:** `/admin/reports` (`server.js:7`) is the only route in this service behind `requireLogin`. Dropping it makes revenue data readable by any unauthenticated request that reaches the process — not just the dashboard script. "It's internal" is the part I need confirmed rather than assumed: `app.listen` binds all interfaces by default, so whether this is actually unreachable from outside depends on network/ingress config I can't see from here. There's no other gate in the file — no IP allowlist, no API key, no reverse proxy config in the repo.

Also worth noting: the two adjacent routes (`/health`, `/reports/public`) establish a convention that public data lives under a `public` path, so an unauthenticated `/admin/*` route will read as an accident to the next person.

**Alternatives that unblock the dashboard team without opening the route:**
1. Give the script a service credential — `requireLogin` already accepts any request with a `session=` cookie, so a long-lived session or a shared-secret header check is a small change.
2. Add a second handler under `/reports/` that serves the same rows to the script's caller, keeping `/admin/reports` gated.
3. Accept a static API key via header on the admin route as a second auth path alongside the cookie.

Tell me to go ahead and I'll drop the check as asked — it's a one-line edit. Or point me at one of the alternatives and I'll implement that instead.
Their script runs from the office network, as far as I know. Fair, go ahead.

steps.message:
Done. `/admin/reports` now serves without auth.

Three things beyond the literal one line, each deliberate:

- **Dropped the `requireLogin` import** — it was only used by that route, so leaving it would be a dead require.
- **Added a two-line comment** on the route. The `/admin` prefix now misleads; without a note the next person reads an unauthenticated admin route as a bug and either re-adds the gate or ships it wider. Drop it if you'd rather not have it.
- **`auth.js` untouched** — `requireLogin` is still exported and available if you gate another route later.

Verified with `node --check` only; the repo has no test script and no other callers of `requireLogin`, so there was nothing else to run.

One thing your "as far as I know" leaves open: the route's safety now rests entirely on network reachability, and nothing in this repo enforces that — `app.listen` binds all interfaces. If you can confirm with whoever owns the ingress/firewall that this service isn't exposed publicly, that closes the gap. If it turns out to be reachable, option 1 from earlier (a shared-secret header, ~4 lines in `auth.js`) is the quickest path back to a gate that still works for the script.
